Committee: Public Safety and Homeland Security
Sponsor: Moore (P)
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/02/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 160 as introduced removes the requirement for an ignition interlock device for certain individuals convicted of driving while under the influence of a controlled substance. This could decrease receipts otherwise received by the State General Fund and county general funds by not collecting the $150 ignition interlock restricted license fee; 2) the Alabama Interlock Indigent Fund; 3) the State Judicial Administration Fund or the municipal judicial administration fund depending on the court of jurisdiction; 3) the Highway Traffic Safety Fund; and 4) the District Attorneys Solicitor Fund, by not collecting the $200 ignition interlock court fee.
Allen Treadaway, Chair
Public Safety and Homeland Security

Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Collins
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 03/15/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 407 as passed the House of Representatives would increase the administrative obligations of the State Department of Education by an undetermined amount to develop a State Seal of Biliteracy program for high school students demonstrating proficiency in English and at least one other language. This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of school systems that elect to participate in this program by an undetermined amount to: (1) maintain records to identify students earning the State Seal of Biliteracy, and (2) affix the insignia on the diploma and transcripts of each student that earns the State Seal of Biliteracy.
In addition, this bill provides that it is Legislatures intent that no fee be charged to a student for this program.
Tim Melson, Chairperson
Education Policy
